label: early original-phase steps (t=1-3), favoring n/f/s after an h/u/v/i/x opener
explanation: Fires only in the original phase at positions t=1-5, with 98% of activation mass at t=1-3 (64% at t=2). It never fires at t=0, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase. Within that window the deciding factor is a combination of tokens: it is most likely when the current token is n or f (also s, c, h, digits 0/1), the token is appearing for the first time, and an earlier token is one of h/u/v/i/x. The strongest activations are n at t=2 after the prefixes v h, h u or h h. The position window alone gives 98% mass recall at 4% precision; the token-conjunction predicate gets dev F1 0.37 and mass recall 0.56. The rest looks like a spread-out lookup over pairs of early tokens that no compact predicate captures.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=h (+4.89), prev_tok=u (+4.53), prev_tok=i (+3.92), prev_tok=v (+3.80), prev_tok=n (+3.73), prev_tok=x (+3.51). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-6.55), in_tok=a (-5.43), in_tok=k (-5.38), in_tok=2 (-5.34).
